extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark dataset for Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) with 9.6K human-written questions and 23.1K machine-generated questions focusing on visual and logical reasoning over real-world charts. The dataset includes 20,882 charts curated from four online sources (Statista, Pew Research, Our World in Data, OECD) to ensure diversity in visual styles and topics. The benchmark addresses complex reasoning questions involving arithmetic and logical operations, visual attribute references, and open-vocabulary answers.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.citeAs: Masry, A., Long, D. X., Tan, J. Q., Joty, S., & Hoque, E. (2022). ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning. arXiv preprint arXiv:2203.10244.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were curated from four online sources (Statista, Pew Research, Our World in Data, OECD) to ensure diversity in visual styles and topics. Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) where workers provided two questions per chart focusing on compositional and visual reasoning. Machine-generated QA pairs were created using a T5 model fine-tuned on SQuAD, applied to human-written chart summaries from Statista, followed by manual validation and cleaning.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Surveys, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Charts were sourced from Statista, Pew Research, Our World in Data (OWID), and OECD. Statista, OWID, and OECD provided underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions. Pew Research provided only chart images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data collection period not explicitly stated in the paper.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data tables were extracted from chart images using a modified ChartOCR pipeline that adapts key-point detection networks to locate chart elements and uses CRAFT for text recognition. Extracted data values were associated with text labels using positional and color information. For pie charts, segment values were estimated by calculating angles between borderlines.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Charts were filtered to ensure diversity in visual styles and topics. Human-authored QA pairs were manually validated for correctness and agreement. Machine-generated QA pairs were filtered using a heuristic to remove unanswerable questions and manually cleaned for the test set. Data tables were structured to include fully-structured data with textual labels and legend associations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk where workers provided two questions per chart focusing on compositional (involving mathematical/logical operations) and visual (referring to visual attributes) reasoning. Answers were validated by another annotator, with exact matches considered correct. Machine-generated QA pairs were created using a T5 model fine-tuned on SQuAD, applied to human-written chart summaries from Statista. Generated questions were filtered using a heuristic to remove unanswerable questions and manually validated for quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for human annotations. T5 model (Raffel et al., 2020) for machine-generated questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between crowd workers for human-authored QA pairs was 61.04% based on exact matches, but increased to 78.55% when considering typos and lexical variations. For machine-generated QA pairs, 86.64% were found to be complete, answerable, and correct after manual analysis of 1,250 samples.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 human annotations per chart for human-authored QA pairs. Machine-generated QA pairs were manually validated for quality.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with an acceptance rate of 95% and total accomplished HITs of 5000 were selected. Workers were compensated at $0.6 USD per task, based on an estimated time of 3-5 minutes per task and the U.S. minimum wage at the time ($7.25 USD per hour). Annotations were anonymized to protect privacy.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: T5 model (Raffel et al., 2020) for question generation from chart summaries. ChartOCR (Luo et al., 2021) for data extraction from chart images, extended to output fully-structured data tables. CRAFT (Baek et al., 2019) for text recognition in chart elements. Detectron2 (Wu et al., 2019) for object detection in VL-T5 model.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/vis-nlp/ChartQA. The paper mentions plans for future updates and extensions but does not specify a formal maintenance or versioning policy.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset does not explicitly mention the collection of personal sensitive information. Charts were sourced from public platforms (Statista, Pew Research, OWID, OECD) and complied with their terms and conditions. Annotators' privacy was protected by anonymizing their annotations.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance Chart Question Answering systems that can assist users in analyzing data visualizations. However, the paper acknowledges that such systems could potentially be misused to mislead the public about chart content and implications. The authors emphasize the need for responsible use of these models.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset includes charts from four online sources (Statista, Pew Research, OWID, OECD), which may introduce biases related to the topics covered (e.g., politics, economy, health, society). The human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk, which may introduce demographic biases among the annotators. The machine-generated QA pairs were created from human-written summaries, which may reflect the linguistic and topical biases present in those summaries.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may not generalize well to all types of charts or visual styles due to the diversity of sources. The performance of models decreases when the gold data table is not provided, highlighting challenges in automatic data extraction from real-world charts. The dataset includes complex reasoning questions that current models struggle to handle, particularly those involving nested operations. The paper notes that the dataset introduces more challenging visual and compositional questions and lexical variations compared to previous datasets.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-tuning for Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) systems. The dataset is designed to evaluate models' ability to answer complex reasoning questions involving arithmetic and logical operations, as well as visual attribute references. The paper suggests that the dataset can be used to pretrain models for related tasks, such as TableQA or Visual Question Answering (VQA).
